title: More Than One Night: Tyson Foods’ Commitment to DC Central Kitchen
summary: Tyson Foods’ partnership with DC Central Kitchen goes beyond Capital Food Fight, supporting food access, culinary job training and economic opportunity.

For the second consecutive year, Tyson Foods had the opportunity to serve as Presenting Sponsor of[DC Central Kitchen](https://dccentralkitchen.org/) ’s[Capital Food Fight](https://capitalfoodfight.org/) . Held November 12 at The Anthem in Washington, D.C., the annual event brought together an incredible mix of chefs, restaurants and supporters around a shared belief in the power of food to make a difference.


And there was plenty to celebrate. More than 1,200 people filled the venue, with a record 87 restaurants and bars participating throughout the evening. Together, the event raised $900,000 for DC Central Kitchen’s hunger-fighting and job training programs.


At the center of the night was the signature chef competition, where four talented local chefs put their creativity to the test. Tyson Foods even had a small part in the competition itself when[aidells® Artichoke & Garlic Smoked Chicken Sausage](https://www.aidells.com/products/lunch-dinner-sausage/00764014613525) appeared as one of the surprise secret ingredients. And, by the end of the night, Chef Brian Lacayo was crowned the 2026 Capital Food Fight champion.


But as exciting as the night was, our connection to DC Central Kitchen reaches far beyond Capital Food Fight.


##### **Food as a Pathway to Opportunity**


What makes our relationship with DC Central Kitchen especially meaningful is the way its work connects food access with job training and economic opportunity.


In 2026 alone, Tyson Foods committed **$300,000** through our Capital Food Fight sponsorship, support of the organization’s Culinary Job Training program and an in-kind donation of **more than 35,000 pounds of nutritious protein** to help provide essential meals.


For the second consecutive year, Tyson Foods is also sponsoring a 14-week Culinary Job Training class for adults facing barriers to employment. The program combines hands-on culinary instruction with career readiness training and real-world experience, preparing students for careers in the food service industry. Students can also work toward industry credentials, while graduates receive continued support as they pursue employment. Over more than 30 years, the program has helped more than 2,000 people launch culinary careers.


For the students currently in the program, some of the most meaningful parts are also the most personal:


> “What I like the most about being in the job training program is, honestly, meeting new people and the experience itself.” – Adrian Young


> “My favorite part of the program is learning to make different dishes in the kitchen.” – Cecilia Dyson


> “DC Central Kitchen is teaching us great life skills.” – Charmaine Bloomfield


> “My favorite thing about DC Central Kitchen is learning kitchen etiquette and getting to work with my teammate.” – Marshall Barrett


Together, their experiences offer a glimpse into the practical skills, career preparation, connections and confidence students are building throughout the program.


##### **A Partnership with Purpose**


The people behind the programs are ultimately what give this partnership its purpose. For our team, seeing that impact firsthand reinforces why supporting DC Central Kitchen goes well beyond a single event.


“One of the things that is the most impressive about DC Central Kitchen is the long-term impact that they have on the lives of individuals in the community where we operate, said Andy York, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs at Tyson Foods.


Capital Food Fight gave us a chance to celebrate that impact. The energy, creativity and, of course, incredible food made for a memorable evening, all in support of a mission that continues long after the event is over.


**More than One Night**


It’s easy to leave Capital Food Fight remembering the incredible food, the friendly competition and the energy inside The Anthem. But the part that stays with you is the purpose behind it all.


That’s what makes our relationship with DC Central Kitchen worth celebrating. Capital Food Fight may bring us together for one memorable night, but the impact it supports continues year-round.


Learn more about[DC Central Kitchen and its work to fight hunger differently](https://dccentralkitchen.org/2026/06/29/tyson-foods-returns-to-2026-capital-food-fight-as-presenting-sponsor/) .
